children.title: About – Data Terra EOSC Node
children.main_text: Data Terra EOSC Node helpdesk@earth-data.eu About Resource hub Service Hub Projects Use Cases Documentation About Resource hub Service Hub Projects Use Cases Documentation A thematic node within the European Open Science Cloud dedicated to Earth system, biodiversity, and environmental sciences About EOSC Node Data Terra Partnership landscape Node Coordination Governance and EOSC alignment Who is it for ? Architecture overview About EOSC Node Data Terra The EOSC Node, powered by Data Terra and NFDI4Earth, is one of the thematic nodes representing the Earth system and environmental sciences within the EOSC Federation. It provides a single, integrated entry point to trusted thematic data and services across Europe, bringing together environmental and Earth system science resources, including Earth Observation data and services. Its key added value lies in federating complementary national ecosystems of expert thematic data hubs across Europe, enabling coherent, interoperable, and science-driven access to the full complexity of the Earth system, from in-situ observations and Earth Observation data to modelling, analysis, and advanced digital services. The EOSC Node Data Terra stands out through several key strengths Delivering a federated architecture layer that facilitates data discovery and integration across disciplines, supporting solutions to complex scientific research challenges Providing seamless access to advanced computing and data-processing resources through shared tools and virtual research environments designed to enable reproducible and collaborative research Offering AI-ready and interoperable datasets across the entire research data lifecycle from discovery and management to analysis and reuse, supporting evidence-based decision-making These contributions lay at the crossroads of major European programmes and infrastructures and are firmly anchored in the principles of Open Science and the free circulation of knowledge. Together, they enable next-generation environmental research and help address major societal challenges, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and global sustainability. EOSC Node Data Terra within the EOSC Federation EOSC Node Data Terra partnership landscape In the framework the EOSC Node, the French Research Infrastructure Data Terra has established a shared vision and collaborative strategy with NFDI4Earth, a key initiative of Germany’s National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI). This collaboration aims to strengthen the European federation’s capabilities for managing and integrating Earth system, environmental, and biodiversity data, while fostering the adoption of advanced, knowledge-driven technologies. Since the 2025 EOSC Federation build-up phase, the EOSC Node Data Terra launched an initiative to broaden its partnership base by engaging organisations and contributors from other EU Member States. The objective is to develop a European transnational thematic node that brings together complementary national expertise, infrastructures, data, and services. Åland Albania Andorra Armenia Austria Azerbaijan Belgium Bulgaria Bosnia and Herz. Belarus Switzerland N. Cyprus Czechia Germany Denmark Algeria Egypt Spain Estonia Finland France Faeroe Is. United Kingdom Georgia Guernsey Greece Greenland Croatia Hungary Isle of Man Ireland Iran Iraq Iceland Israel Italy Jersey Jordan Kazakhstan Lebanon Libya Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Latvia Morocco Moldova North Macedonia Malta Montenegro Netherlands Norway Poland Portugal Palestine Romania Russia Saudi Arabia San Marino Serbia Slovakia Slovenia Sweden Syria Tunisia Turkey Ukraine Kosovo Data Terra Research Infrastructure is a distributed research e-infrastructure organized around five thematic data and service hubs—Atmosphere ( AERIS ), Ocean ( ODATIS ), Land Surfaces ( THEIA ), Solid Earth ( FormaTerre ), and Biodiversity ( PNDB )—complemented by cross-cutting services that promote FAIR data management, satellite data access, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Through its strong integration with national, European and international research infrastructures, Data Terra contributes to a coordinated ecosystem for Earth system observation and environmental research by providing seamless access to data, services and expertise to the scientific community. As a strategic initiative supported by the French Ministry of Research and Higher Education, Data Terra Research Infrastructure plays a pivotal role in structuring and advancing research across these critical domains, with strong partnership with European Research Infrastructure Consortia. RI Data Terra is also the French thematic reference centre for Earth, Climate, Environment and Biodiversity within Research Data Gouv , reflecting its leading role in open science and the development of international data standards. In addition, it is a partner of AI Factory France , led by GENCI, where it coordinates the Earth sciences domain and contributes to strengthening links between AI research, industry, and environmental sciences. NFDI4Earth is Germany’s National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI) consortium for the Earth System Sciences, addressing the digital needs of a broad scientific community working together to understand the Earth’s complex systems and the impacts of global change. As a community-driven initiative, NFDI4Earth brings together universities, research organizations, infrastructure providers, governmental institutions, scientific associations, and networks across Germany. It actively collaborates with national and international partners to promote FAIR research data management, interoperability, and open science. The NFDI4Earth consortium connects a distributed network of partners that develops and provides FAIR, coherent, and open access to Earth system science data, along with innovative research data management and data science methods. Through its integration of expertise, services, and strategic collaborations across research infrastructures and initiatives, NFDI4Earth supports researchers in discovering, accessing, and reusing data while contributing to a coordinated national and international ecosystem for Earth system research. It advances sustainable, open, and interoperable data practices. EOSC Node Data Terra Coordination Legal entity Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique Coordinating organisations National Institute for Earth sciences and Astronomy (INSU) Technische Universität Dresden (TU DRESDEN) Contributing organisations Governance & EOSC Alignment The EOSC Node Data Terra is part of the EOSC Federation and operates in alignment with its principles, standards, and governance framework. The EOSC Association The EOSC Association works to implement EOSC and the EOSC Federation to advance Open Science practices in the interest of creating new knowledge, promoting innovation and reinforcing public trust in science. The EOSC EU Node The EOSC EU Node facilitates the creation of the EOSC Federation, following a system-of-systems approach based on federated research infrastructures. It provides a technical, administrative and interoperability framework for future infrastructure nodes and represents the first operational European-level node of the EOSC Federation promoted by the European Commission. Who is it for ? Built on strong FAIR principles, the node enables users to discover, access, combine, and process heterogeneous data through shared tools and virtual research environments designed for reproducible and collaborative research. It supports use cases such as cross-domain data integration for climate and biodiversity impact studies, environmental risk monitoring, and FAIR-by-design workflows. Researchers Access FAIR data, tools and services for scientific analysis Data Scientists and Engineers Integrate and develop interoperable data products across infrastructures eInfrastructures Contribute thematic services and resources to the EOSC ecosystem Policy & Decision Makers Leverage environmental data for informed decisions Architecture overview The EOSC Node’s digital gateway serves as a single-entry point to the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC), facilitating access to open science resources and services across Europe. The EOSC Node Data Terra architecture builds on existing e-infrastructures, frameworks and initiatives, including the GAIA Data e-Infrastructure and NFDI4Earth , and leverages the outcomes of previous projects such as FAIR-EASE, as well as ongoing projects developed within the EOSC framework. As an EOSC Node, Data Terra provides single sign-on access to high-quality, trusted, FAIR and AI-ready multi-domain data for the Earth system. It also provides cross-domain data analysis workflows and Virtual Research Environments (VREs), enabling multidisciplinary collaboration and facilitating the federation and reuse of distributed resources across the EOSC ecosystem. children.title: A Propos – Data Terra EOSC Node
children.main_text: Data Terra EOSC Node Connexion À propos Hub de ressources Hub de services Projets Cas d’usage Documentation À propos Hub de ressources Hub de services Projets Cas d’usage Documentation Un noeud thématique au sein de l’European Open Science Cloud dédié au système terrestre, à la biodiversité et aux sciences de l’environnement Comment ça a commencé Coordination C’est pour qui ? Architecture overview Gouvernance et alignement des CEE Les origines Les Nœud de données Terra EOSC s’intègre profondément aux infrastructures nationales de recherche numérique en France, assurant un soutien solide à la recherche à forte intensité de données dans le système de la Terre, l’environnement, la biodiversité et les sciences liées au climat. En tant qu’initiative stratégique soutenue par le ministère français de la recherche et de l’enseignement supérieur, Infrastructure de recherche Data Terra joue un rôle central dans la structure et l’avancement de la recherche dans ces domaines critiques, avec un partenariat solide avec Consortium européen sur les infrastructures de recherche. Data Terra est une infrastructure de recherche distribuée organisée autour de cinq données thématiques et centres de services—Atmosphère ( aeris ), Océan ( odatis ), les surfaces terrestres ( Theia ), terre solide ( formateur ), et la biodiversité ( PNDB )—Complètement par des services transversaux qui favorisent la gestion équitable des données, l’accès aux données satellitaires et la collaboration interdisciplinaire. Grâce à sa forte intégration avec les infrastructures de recherche nationales, européennes et internationales, Data Terra contribue à un écosystème coordonné pour l’observation du système terrestre et la recherche environnementale en fournissant un accès transparent aux données, aux services et à l’expertise à la communauté scientifique. quelque chose à propos de ndfi4earth Coordination des nœuds Terra EOSC Organisation de coordination France Institut national des sciences de la Terre et de l’astronomie pour Centre national de la recherche scientifique Organismes contributeurs C'est pour qui ? Des chercheurs Accéder à des données, outils et services équitables pour l'analyse scientifique Data Scientists et ingénieurs Intégrer et développer des produits de données interopérables à travers les infrastructures eInfrastructures Apporter des services et des ressources thématiques à l'écosystème de l'EOSC Politiques et décideurs Tirer parti des données environnementales pour des décisions éclairées Architecture overview La passerelle numérique de l'EOSC Node sert de point d'entrée unique au European Open Science Cloud (EOSC), facilitant l'accès à des ressources et des services scientifiques ouverts à travers l'Europe. L’architecture de nœuds Data Terra EOSC est construite sur des structures et des ressources existantes, telles que le Infrastructure de données GAIA initiative, et tire parti des résultats de la simpliste Projet. En tant que nœud eOSC, Data Terra fournit une connexion unique pour des données multi-domaines fiables, fiables, équitables et prêtes à l’emploi pour le système terrestre. Il fournit également un flux de travail d’analyse de données inter-domaines et des VRE permettant une collaboration multidisciplinaire en tirant parti des ressources fédérées. En savoir plus sur le nœudCapacités S Gouvernance et alignement des CEE Le nœud Data Terra eOSC fait partie de la fédération eOSC et fonctionne conformément à ses principes, normes et cadre de gouvernance.
